svg.aria-label: jukecord's parts, from the outside in. Four ways in: the panel in a browser and the jukecord command call the HTTP API, whose requests pass Access, which decides who may do it and in which server, on their way to the actions; Discord's slash commands go to the actions directly. The actions, one function per thing a person can do, ask the resolver to turn an address or search words into tracks, and drive each server's queue and player. The player is the clock: it sends the voice channel the music, has the preparer run yt-dlp and ffmpeg into Ogg Opus in the media cache, and with the queue tells the event bus about every change. Browsers playing along get each change over a WebSocket, made once for all of them, and the audio from the cache with Range requests. The queues, the players and the actions keep their state in SQLite. Rainbow lines are the music people hear.

the same for all four ways in
